questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses and the destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest. I had to figure out most things by myself as the guidance and help for erasmus students was lacking a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a general introduction but after that if you had a problem there was not much help to find. For example my coordinator never answered my mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the site Spotahome, which works great.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: well you can't really live on campus in Almería.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not easy. I wasn't completely registered in the system until april because I had to change a subject and so there were many problems with getting my OLA accepted. And here I lacked a lot of guidance and help from so-called coordinators at both my home and host university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration in itself before getting there was fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mostly asked former students for help and then my coordinator at home.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: succesfull, but it was more a problem changing subject.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient, but also don't be afraid to write and ask both your home and host university if you are not hearing anything back.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some classes I have been very satisfied by and others really lacked a lot both academically and structurally.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. At UCPH there is a lot more opportunity for active participation and critical thinking whereas at UAL, some classes were just the profesor doing a powerpoint and then ending class early.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Usos especializados del español
Fundamentos de la lingüística general
Literatura y género
Historia de los movimientos sociales en la España contemporánea
Historia del mundo actual

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I have really enjoyed the course Literatura y Género where i had a passionate and structured profesor who cared a lot about the content of her course. She took our participation serious and encouraged us to participate and have our own voice as much as possible. The class was very interesting and i learned a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was expensive to buy a used bike, but there is a chance that we got scammed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many beautiful beaches nearby and a lot of nice spots to go out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A spot I went to a lot was La Guajira which is a social-cultural club were they do a lot of different events such as language exchange, jam-sessions, flamenco, bachata and salsa classes, + a lot more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: La Guajira because it's free and very versatile. It was always a good experience to got there. Also it has a rooftop overlooking the city and the Alcazaba.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the beaches of course. Go to Cabo de Gata for example, which is a nice and calm beach area just an hour away by bus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy in some aspects but harder in others.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to as many of the introduction events as possible as this is a very good opportunity to meet and connect with the other students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: one thing I found challenging was the lack of awareness of the space around you that i experienced a lot of spanish people had. Both on the bike path but also just walking through town.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: i learned to appreciate the slow living and flow of everything and started to question myself often why I was in such a hurry.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Inform yourself the best you can, and read the descriptions of the course you choose thoroughly.
2. Check the times of the different classes before choosing them, because there will be time table conflicts. 
3. The best thing you can do if you are lost with anything is to ask, and the spanish people are very friendly and more often than not willing to help.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: enjoy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the many different people from all over the world that i met and the friendships that i made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: probably the exams. It was very stressfull and I had multiple exams in one day.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no.

questions.answer: Yes
